ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The International Company must engage a licensed registered agent who is a reporting entity under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018. The agent must conduct mandatory customer due diligence (CDD) prior to the incorporation filing. The protocol mandates screening against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and Samoa domestic Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) sanctions and PEP databases. All UBOs and officers must be screened and the result documented in the CDD file. The FIU Act 2018 requires submission of suspicious transaction reports (STRs) within prescribed timeframes and enhanced due diligence (EDD) for PEPs. Screening must be repeated on amendments to beneficial ownership records and on any trigger event (e.g., intended opening of credit card merchant facilities with local banks such as ANZ Samoa Limited, BSP Samoa Limited or Samoa Commercial Bank).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Registrar of International Companies online portal (Samoa International Companies Registry, apolima.mcil.gov.ws or the official names reservation e-filing facility of Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA))
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name must be in the English alphabet or in a language using the Latin alphabet transliterated into English spelling. The official corporate name must end with the word 'Limited' or the abbreviation 'Ltd' (other approved suffixes include Corporation, Incorporated, Public Limited Company, Société Anonyme or their abbreviations, subject to approval). The Chinese business name may be reserved and displayed as a transliteration in the company records; however, the statutory registered name for all legal acts is the English/Latin alphabet version. Transliteration must be an exact phonetic equivalent and cannot be a surname-only designation. Where a Chinese trade description is used as a business name, it must not convey similar meaning to a protected name on the Registry and must not contain any prohibited token.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Holding Company (when indicating a regulated financial group)
broker or any token implying the conduct of financial services business
any name that implies a connection with the Samoan Government or any overseas government
any word that contradicts public policy or Samoan customs
Any expression with 'Specialty Tea Salon Lounge' is permissible but must not be similar to a previously registered entity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the registrant may apply for an administrative review by filing a notice of appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 21 days of the notice of refusal. The notice must be delivered in writing, stating the ground of objection and a certified copy of the proposed name, together with any evidence of consent from a relevant regulatory body if the name contains a restricted token. The Registrar shall give a written determination within 14 days of receipt of the appeal. If the appeal is dismissed, further recourse lies with the Supreme Court of Samoa under the International Companies Act 1987, Section 13(6) on a point of law or through a fresh name reservation application with an altered acceptable name. For the 'Specialty Tea Salon Lounge' designation, the registered agent should pre-screen against the existing Registry index and, if the name is rejected on similarity grounds, the permissible practice is to append a unique numeric suffix or distinctive business descriptor before resorting to formal appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for International Company. The International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa) requires the registered office to be at the physical office address of a licensed registered agent in Samoa. A virtual office in the sense of a non-Samoan mailbox cannot satisfy the registered office requirement. However, the physical business operations of the specialty tea salon lounge may lawfully be conducted entirely outside Samoa; the registered office serves rigidly as the legal address for service of process. Any commercial presence in Samoa itself (should the owner later onshore the salon) must have a separate physical location licensed under the Business Names Act and the Business Licence Act 1998. Virtual office for IBC (International Company) specifically is not permitted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a tax-exempt offshore International Company with no on-island business license for a tea salon, the likelihood of unannounced physical inspection is Low (less than 10% per year). The risk rating rises to approximately 45–60% per year if the company obtains a local business license and operates the specialty tea lounge in-person in Samoa, because the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) and Samoa Revenue Authority conduct periodic spot-inspection campaigns of hospitality premises for trade, liquor, food-safety, customs and excise compliance. For the incorporated offshore structure, the registered agent office is subject to inspection under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 and the International Companies Act 1987; inspection is largely triggered by suspicious transaction reports or CDD file reviews. Given the Low_Risk_Standard tier and that the tea salon does not involve regulated banking activity, the SDN/OFC inspection probability from the offshore Unit is 10% over the initial 2-year period; if merchant card services are opened with a local bank, that does not increase physical inspections but raises the FIU's remote monitoring of risk transparency.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended — ss. 4-12 (incorporation procedure), s. 25 (articles of incorporation), s. 31 (registered office), s. 42 (registered agent), ss. 52-58 (directors and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association endorsed by Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an International Company; the Company may incorporate with nil or nominal capital and no escrow deposit requirement. Authorized capital must be declared in the Articles, and tax-exempt election may be recorded in the Articles without capital attestation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Company subscribes to and accepts the whole of the share capital allotted by the Subscriber in the Memorandum of Association and that the directors, acting collectively, are hereby authorized to issue and allot shares in one or more classes as the business plan requires. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office of the Company be established at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and that the registered agent be retained as the statutory agent for service of process. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the following persons be and are hereby appointed as the first directors of the Company: [set out full names]. The Company Secretary and resident officer appointments are confirmed, and the directors are authorized to open bank accounts and execute all incorporation completion filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the prescribed Name Reservation Application through a SIFA-licensed registered agent. The proposed name must be materially distinct from names on the Samoa corporate register and must include a limited liability suffix or equivalent designation. Pay the name reservation fee and obtain the Registrar's written clearance before lodgment of the Articles.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copy of the appointing subscriber
Engagement letter with licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the applicant resubmits an amended application within 7 business days or appeals to the Registrar for review; an approved name lapses unless incorporation is completed within 30 days of clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed International Company Service Provider / Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English for a tax-exempt International Company limited by shares. The subscriber executes the Articles, and the registered agent countersigns its statutory consent to act. The tax-exempt status election and the authorized capital schedule are recorded in the Articles.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: SIFA drafting comments are addressed through a written response memorandum; any required amendment is executed by the subscriber and the corrected execution page is filed with the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of International Companies, SIFA filing counter or e-registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles, name clearance certificate, registered agent consent, incorporator declaration, and the official filing fee of USD 250. The Registrar examines the instrument for conformity with sections 4 to 12 of the International Companies Act 1987.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a request for information, the applicant rectifies omissions within 14 calendar days; if the filing is deemed defective, the registered agent files a corrective affidavit and the application is summarily reviewed by the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the Certificate of Incorporation and the certified copy of the registered Articles. Open the statutory registers of members, directors, officers, and charges; prepare and issue share certificates to initial subscribers and record the formal incorporation date.
required_dossiers: Statutory Register of Directors and Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any typographical discrepancy in the Certificate is cured by the Registrar's certificate of correction filed through the registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Governance Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office of the Company, Apia; meeting conducted by unanimous written resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution covering share subscription, adoption of the registered office, appointment of directors and officers, corporate seal approval, and authorization to open bank accounts. The registered agent records the resolution in the statutory minute book.
required_dossiers: Waiver of notice and unanimous written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a physical quorum cannot be formed, a written resolution signed by all first directors is treated as a valid meeting of the board under the Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commencement of Industrial, Public Health and Environmental Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Health - Food Safety Unit; Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment - Planning and Urban Management Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Food Business Premises Application for the specialty tea salon together with the environmental screening form, stamped floor plan, drainage diagram, and fire escape layout. Physical operations may not commence until the Food Premises Operating Permit and occupancy clearances are granted.
required_dossiers: Stamped floor plan and fire escape diagram
Building and electrical clearance certificates from MWTI
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the sanitary or building inspection identifies non-compliance, the company carries out corrective works and requests re-inspection within 10 business days; a refusal may be appealed to the Licensing Committee of the Ministry of Health.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health - National Food Safety and Hygiene Licensing Unit, in coordination with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: National Food Premises Operating Permit (Food Hygiene License) for Specialty Tea Salon and Lounge

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Screening-Level Environmental Registration; Full EIA Report waived for premises under 500 square meters with negligible industrial discharge
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Samoa national water quality standards under the Water Resources Management Act 2008: wastewater BOD below 50 mg/L; no VOCs or process air emissions from tea preparation; solid waste handled under approved commercial waste disposal contract; stormwater discharge strictly segregated from sanitary effluent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA); building structural load inspection and occupancy certificate from the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI); electrical installation clearance; workplace health and safety registration with the Department of Labour.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue, Samoa (Inland Revenue Division); online portal: eRevenue / Samoa Tax Administration System (TAS)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC): (1) incorporate with the Samoa International Companies Office (ICO); (2) file the certificate of incorporation and a certified registry extract with the Inland Revenue Division to obtain a Samoan Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for administrative purposes; (3) if the IC commences a taxable activity in Samoa or supplies taxable goods/services to Samoan residents, register for Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) within 21 days of commencement of activity or once the WST 80,000 registration threshold is met; (4) an IC that remains wholly offshore and does not trade with Samoan residents may be treated as a nil-assessable non-resident entity and is not required to file VAGST returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available under Samoan law. The International Companies Act 1987 confers a statutorily insulated offshore tax-exempt status. An IC may elect to convert to or redomicile as a Samoan Domestic Company under the Companies Act 2001, which would subject it to income tax and VAGST. Hybrid mismatch rules are not adopted in Samoa, and no tax election can produce deductible shareholder payments or otherwise alter the IC's exempt classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax, Samoa GST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 80,000 (Eighty thousand Samoan Tala) annual taxable turnover
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time electronic invoicing clearance or cryptographic fiscal stamping regime is currently in force. VAGST-registered suppliers must issue tax invoices in a form approved by the Commissioner of Inland Revenue, retain source documents for seven years, and file electronic periodic VAGST returns. The Ministry of Revenue is progressively deploying an online invoice verification and electronic payments portal, but there is no API-connected fiscal device mandate and no digital stamping requirement yet.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods are zero-rated when the goods are physically exported from Samoa and delivered to a destination outside Samoa within 28 days of the supply. Services, including high-end tea-service and lounge hospitality supplied to non-resident cruise or airline clients, are zero-rated when supplied under a contract with a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time of performance, or when the services are performed on goods located outside Samoa. The supplier must retain export evidence, a non-resident recipient declaration, a tax invoice marked 'Zero-Rated Export,' and proof of the export destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank debit confirmation evidencing settlement of export proceeds in a Samoan bank account
Original VAGST tax invoice marked 'Zero-Rated Export'
Non-resident recipient declaration and proof of export destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rated export claims are disallowed and treated as taxable output tax. The Commissioner may retrospectively claw back VAGST refunds, impose a late-payment penalty of up to 5% per month plus interest, and assess a shortfall penalty up to 150% of the tax evaded. Deliberate furnishing of false export documentation is a criminal offence carrying a fine not exceeding WST 100,000 and possible imprisonment up to ten years under the Samoa Tax Administration Act 2011. The International Company's tax-exempt status does not shield these penalties where the exporter seeks VAGST refunds on improperly claimed zero-rated supplies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), in coordination with the Samoa International Finance Authority for international company licensing and offshore banking matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tālā (WST) is a managed-floating currency administered under the Exchange Control Act 1977. Current-account transactions, including trade payments, service fees, and visa-related settlements, are freely permitted through licensed authorized dealers upon documentary support. Capital-account operations, including equity injections, intercompany loans, and profit distribution, require CBS exchange control approval and are scrutinized for source-of-funds, economic substance, and repatriation capacity. For an International Company (IC) conducting a physical specialty tea salon lounge serving local consumers, the presumption of offshore exemption under the International Companies Act 1988 is diminished; profit remittance is permissible only after audited financial statements, valid tax clearance, and registration of the IC as a licensed local business are confirmed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Act 1977 and subsidiary Exchange Control Regulations, exporters must repatriate foreign currency receipts to Samoa within 180 days of shipment and surrender 100% of the proceeds to a CBS-licensed authorized dealer for conversion into WST at the prevailing interbank rate. Specific exemptions may be granted by the Central Bank of Samoa for international companies operating under a valid offshore business certificate; however, a domestic-facing tea salon and lounge cannot rely on such exemptions and must strictly comply with the 180-day repatriation and full-surrender requirement for any export revenue derived from tea product resale.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-nil statutory viability. Samoa has no domestically recognized electronic money institution (EMI) licensing regime; offshore digital banks, non-bank EMI providers, and unlicensed payment aggregators are not permitted to open host accounts or issue virtual IBANs for Samoan International Companies. A licensed offshore fintech may only interact with the local clearing system through a CBS-authorized dealer, and can never provide a standalone treasury account without a Samoan commercial bank partner. For the specialty tea salon lounge, fintech EMIs should be used solely as downstream card-acquiring or FX quotation utilities, not as primary liquidity rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: CBS-tier banks require at least one director or a formally appointed authorized representative with powers of attorney to attend an in-branch onboarding interview during initial account opening. Fully remote account opening is not generally available; however, a private-banking client of the same bank may use a video-verified correspondent onboarding process where the director is already known to the institution, provided all corporate records, resolutions, and beneficial ownership declarations are notarized, apostilled, and submitted before account activation. The IC must also demonstrate its physical Samoan business address for the tea lounge.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity arising from nominee shareholders or a family trust holding the IC's shares.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered agent certificate, full IC register with ultimate beneficial owner schedule, notarized trust deed or trustee resolution, source-of-wealth statement from the settlor, and a 24-month banking reference from the remitting jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border settlement from high-risk jurisdictions or unexpected routing through non-correspondent entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction chain-of-funds ledger, 12 months of bank statements, original trade invoices tied to ISIC 5630 tea salon operations, passport and residential proof for each beneficial owner, and a clear sanctions/PEAC-scope screening report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified physical trading address for the specialty tea salon and lounge.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized commercial lease agreement, Samoan business license or Certificate of Registration, dated photographs of the salon entrance and POS equipment, utility invoice matching the leased address, and VAT or turnover confirmation if filing locally.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-heavy POS sales inconsistent with expected tea lounge revenue patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: POS transaction reconciliation logs, registered cash-register reports, supplier invoices for loose-leaf tea and ceramics, monthly sales declarations to the Ministry of Revenue, and a documented cash management and anti-money-laundering procedure manual.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing requires an external corporate bank to transmit a SWIFT MT103 credit to the IC's WST/USD settlement account held at a CBS-licensed authorized dealer. The incoming payment must quote a valid Exchange Control Application reference issued by the accepting Samoan bank and be categorized under an inward-investment purpose code covering equity subscription or shareholder loan. Capital injections intended for working capital must first be lodged to a Capital Escrow Account, converted to WST after the authorizing dealer confirms CBS approval for amounts exceeding the applicable exchange control threshold, and then released through the Operational Account. The accepting bank must file post-investment reporting with the Central Bank of Samoa within five business days of credit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade-related disbursements flow primarily over SWIFT MT103 for recurring low-value supplier payments—such as loose-leaf tea purchases and ceramic dinnerware—accompanied by proforma invoices and CBS-compliant narrative purpose codes. Commercial Letters of Credit are used for high-value consolidated shipments, with the advising bank issuing SWIFT MT700/MT710 messages and the IC's account charged against a pre-approved FX line. Domestic WST settlements, including payroll, lease payments, and local vendor fees, clear through Samoa's local bank transfer and retail POS acquiring systems; the IC should maintain a separate WST operational account to avoid mixing foreign-currency trade settlement with on-island cash flows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards with an authorized dealing bank, maximum tenor twelve months, covered by a signed CSA and underlying trade documentation

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on WST through an international prime broker where the CBS regulatory framework permits offshore price discovery, used only to hedge committed foreign-currency payables
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps with a CBS-licensed bank for term funding facilities, subject to central bank approval and strict commercial-hedge documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form AR) with annual government licence fee payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of 10% per month or part-month on the unpaid licence fee; arrears exceeding 3 months allow the Registrar to strike the company off the International Companies Register after gazette notice; assets vest in the Public Trustee and directors remain personally liable for pre-strike-off obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) confirmation and AML/KYC attestation schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent and the Registrar of International Companies (SIFA) under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 14 days after the incorporation anniversary; each share transfer triggers a supplementary UBO update filing within 14 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director or officer fines up to SAT 100,000 (approx. USD 35,000) and/or imprisonment; the registered agent must file a suspicious matter report for material UBO discrepancies; continuing omissions may support administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Office and Registered Agent continuation confirmation (including any change notices)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually concurrent with the Annual Return; actual changes of office or agent must be filed within 14 days of the change event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failing to maintain a licensed registered agent is a continuing breach of the International Companies Act 1987 that can trigger administrative strike-off without the standard arrears grace period; directors may face separate personal penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Samoa International Company is exempt from compulsory audit when it has no more than 25 shareholders and has not made a public offer of its shares or debentures. A mandatory independent audit is triggered if the shareholder count exceeds 25, the company has made a public offer of securities, or the Registrar or holders of at least 10% of issued shares lawfully require one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by Samoa; Section 120 of the International Companies Act 1987 requires the IC to keep accounting records that correctly explain transactions and permit preparation of financial statements giving a true and fair view, but audit-exempt ICs are not required to file financial statements with SIFA.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each incorporation anniversary the licensed registered agent issues a UBO confirmation schedule; directors must verify and certify the identity, nationality and proportionate ownership interest of every ultimate beneficial owner, and the agent files the confirmation with the Registrar. Any share transfer during the year requires simultaneous updating of the Register of Members and the UBO Register, with written notice to the agent within 14 days of the transfer; a transfer not so recorded is not recognized for SIFA compliance purposes and blocks issuance of the annual certificate of good standing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share ledger including UBO cross-reference)
Register of Directors and Company Secretary

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$800 - US$1,500 per annum (licensed Samoan CSP covering registered office address, registered agent, Annual Return preparation, UBO confirmation and compliance monitoring)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required for the audit-exempt specialty tea salon IC (no more than 25 shareholders, no public offer); if an audit is lawfully demanded, US$3,000 - US$6,000 per annum for an IFRS-based certified audit of the holding entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (International Company tax exemption; Samoa resident domestic corporate rate is 25%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are exempt from Samoa income tax on foreign-source income. No capital gains tax, no dividend distribution tax, and no branch profit remittance tax. Registration and annual licensing fees replace income tax liabilities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Form IC-AR) filed electronically via the Samoa Ministry of Revenue / Registrar of International Companies online e-services portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation; where the International Company has a taxable resident branch, the CIT return is due within 6 months after the financial year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the International Company
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter exact name from Certificate of Incorporation; no translations or trade names permitted
Enter the unique number assigned by the Samoa International Companies Registry

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office and licensed registered agent in Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the physical Samoa address and the name of the licensed registered agent; a PO Box alone is insufficient
Listing resident directors is optional but the registered agent must remain licensed; non-resident directors may be natural persons or International Companies

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital structure and ultimate beneficial owner declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all natural persons holding 25% or more; for non-resident owners submit passport and proof of address with the declaration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of no Samoa-source business activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs must certify zero income from Samoa domestic trading; specialty tea salon operations must occur outside Samoa or meet the International Companies Act restrictions
Confirm the IC claims the International Company tax exemption and has not elected to be taxed as a domestic company
Pay the statutory Government fee plus registration agent fee; late payment triggers a penalty and possible administrative strike-off

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of WST 500 plus daily/monthly surcharges up to WST 100 per month; continuation of default may result in the International Company being struck off the register, assets escheated, and directors and shareholders exposed to personal liability for unpaid fees and taxes.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions by an exempt International Company; if taxable domestic company, statutory rate is 15% on dividends paid to non-residents
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident payee must submit a Samoa Withholding Tax Treaty Rate Reduction Application (Form WT-2) to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue before remittance, attaching: (1) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the residence jurisdiction; (2) a declaration of beneficial ownership; and (3) supporting bank and contract documentation. Approval is issued as a tax relief certificate. Retroactive claims are only processed by refund after a full tax return filing and may require a longer audit period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates are 15% for royalties and 15% for interest. Treaty rates vary: arm's-length interest is commonly reduced to 5% and royalties to 10% under an applicable DTA, provided the beneficial owner is a resident of the treaty counterparty and no permanent establishment exists in Samoa.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: WST 2,000,000 (for taxable domestic entities only; International Company tax-exempt status does not generate transfer pricing filing obligations, but supporting retention of arm's-length records is advisory)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations apply to relevant entities engaged in geographically mobile activities (banking, insurance, shipping, IP holding, financing, distribution, service centers). A specialty tea salon lounge is not a relevant activity, but the International Company must still maintain a Samoa registered agent, comply with the International Companies Act prohibition on domestic business with Samoa residents, and avoid being treated as a shell company where actual management and commercial substance are wholly outside Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing an International Company annual return that falsely declares no Samoa-source income while the entity derives rental, sales, royalty, or service revenue from Samoa-based customers, tea wholesale, or franchise fees arising in Samoa
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Back assessment of 25% corporate income tax plus penalties of up to 200% of tax evaded; fines up to WST 100,000; mandatory strike-off of the International Company and forfeiture of assets used in the offense
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers knowingly signing a false declaration are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, civil restitution of shifted profits, and may face imprisonment of up to 7 years and travel bans pending investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the International Company as a pure pass-through treasury or branding shell without any real decision-making, registered agent oversight, or legitimate commercial purpose while repatriating profits to non-residents without record of substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Immediate reclassification as a taxable domestic company, repeal of the tax exemption, imposition of 25% corporate tax on all accumulated profits, interest at 10% per annum, and a penalty of WST 50,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil, making shareholders and directors personally liable for the entire tax assessment, bank account freezing, disgorgement of dividends received, and a prohibition from serving as director of any Samoa company for 10 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Breach of Beneficial Ownership Rules
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file beneficial ownership data with the licensed registered agent, using nominee shareholders without proper disclosure, or transacting with sanctioned persons through the tea salon's credit card / POS payment rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties of up to WST 250,000; enforced closure of the registered office; suspension of the licensed agent; referral to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit for criminal anti-money-laundering prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be criminally indicted for money laundering, fined up to WST 500,000, and imprisoned for up to 14 years; assets in Samoa and foreign bank accounts may be seized under confiscation orders

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a specialty tea salon, import-export loose-leaf tea distribution, or hospitality lounge within Samoa using an International Company license instead of required domestic business, trading, and food services licenses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Forfeiture of all revenue earned by the unlicensed business, daily penalty of WST 1,000 from the date of the violation, cancellation of the International Company certificate, and prohibition on future registration for 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unpaid license fees, consumer refunds, and government fines; egregious violations may result in custodial sentences of up to 5 years and personal disqualification from managing any Samoan entity
